title: The phrasing grammar
goal: One stroke for a whole phrase: who on the left, when on the vowels, not on the star, the verb on the right.

blocks.x: One stroke writes a whole phrase

Today a phrase is two words whose keys do not collide ({{of the}} is [[of the|-FT]]). That cannot reach the most-said pairs: *I* is [[I|EU]], whose vowels clash with almost every verb. The grammar gives each part of the phrase its own region of the board, so every combination is one stroke and none overlap. [[it was|KPWHEB]] is *it* + past + *be*; [[I know|SWR-PB]] is *I* + *know*.

**In the dictionary.** All 3,758 phrases are entries of `02-lyk-phrasing.json`, built from `rules/grammar.toml` and deployed with the rest. Lookup finds them: type `I was`, `they wouldn't` or a stroke such as `SWRAB`, and it names the starter, auxiliary, not and verb keys. Full rules: [the phrasing grammar](#/ref/phrases/the-phrasing-grammar).

blocks.x: About 36 things to learn (8 starters, 5 modals with `E` and `*`, 3 special verbs, 20 verbs) give 3,758 phrases. A phrase is one stroke in steno order: starter, vowels and star, verb.

A starter is a left-bank chord the grammar owns: its phrases are fixed before any word settles, so a phrase never takes a word's stroke (the few words whose own candidates landed on one moved to another outline).

blocks.x: `E` is the past everywhere: *could* is *can* in the past, *would* is *will*'s, *should* is *shall*'s, *might* is *may*'s, as in English. The star means *not* and nothing else in a phrase.

items: Go down the verbs from the commonest. A verb's code is its **final consonants** on the right bank, as the rules write them: *get* [[-T]], *come* [[-PL]], *want* [[-PBT]], *find* [[-PBD]], *think* [[-PBG]].
If the word ends in a vowel, use its **first** consonant instead: *say* [[-S]], *go* [[-G]], *know* [[-PB]].
If a commoner verb already has that code, add the verb's **first consonant**: *take* [[-BGT]] (*make* has [[-BG]]); *feel* [[-FL]] (*tell* has [[-L]]).
If that is taken too, add [[-Z]]: *see* [[-SZ]], *like* [[-BLGZ]].

blocks.x: *be* [[-B]], *go* [[-G]] and *think* [[-PBG]] are the same keys as those words' own right-bank sounds in lyk. *have been* [[-FB]] is *have* plus *be*.
